correctness.rationale: The maximizing-ball shift-and-shrink argument establishes preservation of every permissible unimodal peak for all n>=3 and all nonnegative real inputs. The reflected argument handles the descending branch. With h=f(p), endpoint prefix/suffix averages give Mf(0)-f(0)>=A/(p+1) and Mf(n-1)-f(n-1)>=B/(n-p). Telescoping variation gives the claimed gap. For interior p and nonconstant f the gap is strictly positive; at an endpoint the equality condition forces all other entries to the constant minimum. Every endpoint spike attains (n-1)/n. Verified analytically and by 13,652 exact enumerated unimodal profiles (n=3..10, four-value alphabet) plus four exact rational profiles. Finite verification is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The closest verified case proves the conjectured sharp factor only for monotone data. The new statement covers every single-peak sequence, even with strictly increasing and decreasing branches, and adds peak preservation, an interior-peak deficit, and equality rigidity. Primary arXiv:2603.12462v1 introduces the unrestricted path conjecture but does not resolve the unimodal class. Bilz--Weigt treats distinct settings and restricted functions, not the finite-path sharp 1-1/n theorem on arbitrary positive one-hump data. This is a qualified priority judgment; differently indexed literature remains a risk.
residual_risks: Undiscovered earlier single-hump graph maximal theorem under alternate terminology would affect historical priority.
The preservation of unimodality is elementary but the formal bibliographic review is bounded, not a uniqueness certificate.
The universal unrestricted multi-peak conjecture remains unproved.

value.rationale: The precise open inequality on path graphs motivates the natural complete single-hump class as the first nonmonotone test. The structural preservation-of-peak lemma reduces the total variation exactly to endpoint values, while an explicit p-dependent gap quantifies strict suboptimality of interior peaks. This gives an all-n sharp coefficient, all equality cases and an obstruction any proposed multi-peak counterexample must cross. It supplies a meaningful structural extension beyond previously known monotone cases without claiming the unrestricted conjecture.
